data.title: A GPU Calculator That Helps Calculate What GPU to Use
data.author: chlobunnee
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VRAM计算器的有效性、功能和局限性，以及对不同硬件（如NVIDIA和AMD）的支持。

不同观点：
• **支持特定计算器的观点**：[zargon]认为https://apxml.com/tools/vram-calculator 更全面，特别是它能够理解不同模型的注意力机制，并支持量化和KV缓存的计算。但也提到该工具仅支持特定模型，而通用计算器由于模型架构差异往往不准确。

• **对计算器准确性的批评**：[kouteiheika]指出该计算器对训练内存的估算极不准确，尤其是在FP32、BF16、8-bit Adam等技术使用上。例如，训练14B参数模型实际仅需24GB VRAM，而计算器却估算3.77B参数模型需要62GB VRAM。[kouteiheika]认为通过一些优化技巧可以大幅降低VRAM使用。

• **对计算器实用性的质疑**：[funfunfunction]认为该工具可能是为GPU经销商做的廉价营销噱头，暗示其可信度不高。

• **对AMD支持的关注**：[amstan]和[jjmarr]等提到该计算器缺少对AMD硬件的支持，并指出在实际使用中AMD硬件可以运行大型模型，而Nvidia GPU却不一定足够，这显示了对更多硬件支持的需求。

• **对模型选择的困惑**：[mdaniel]对需要手动输入大量模型数据表示困惑，并认为计算结果不明确，降低了工具的实用性。

• **对具体GPU型号缺失的疑问**：[amanzi]和[timothyduong]提到某些具体GPU型号（如RTX 5060 Ti和3090）未被提及，质疑它们是否适用或为何被排除。

• **对计算器功能的建议**：[daft_pink]建议增加导入标准模型的功能，以便用户了解运行流行模型所需的GPU。[chlobunnee]则介绍了自己开发的计算器，并寻求反馈，希望进一步改进功能。

• **对训练大型模型的需求**：[amelius]提到在选择LLama 3 70B模型后，计算器显示所有GPU都不足以支持训练，反映了计算器在处理超大模型时的局限性。

补充讨论：
• **对游戏需求的偏离话题**：[nottorp]提到了游戏如《巫师4》和《死亡搁浅》的GPU需求，偏离了计算器的主要用途，显示出部分用户对工具用途的误解。

• **对NVIDIA偏重的批评**：[snvzz]指出该工具更像是NVIDIA专用计算器，忽视了其他品牌如AMD。

总结：评论主要围绕VRAM计算器的准确性、功能和硬件支持展开，一些用户提供了实际使用经验，另一些则关注特定功能和硬件支持的不足。

data.title: Against the censorship of adult content by payment processors
data.author: SlackingOff123
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一个拥有毛绒兽设的博主在其博客上不仅谈论与毛绒粉丝文化相关的内容，还涉及应用密码学等技术话题。博主提到，当其技术性文章在Hacker News或Reddit上被分享时，常有人对其博客上的毛绒艺术作品持批评态度，称其为“色情”。文章进一步探讨了支付处理机构被用作审查网络自由表达的工具，特别是针对成人内容和边缘群体内容。博主以Collective Shout和Exodus Cry等组织为例，指出这些组织通过向支付处理机构施压来实现审查目的，尽管它们声称维护道德或女权主义，但其反LGBTQ和反堕胎的立场引发了质疑。文章强调，这种审查手段可能被其他团体效仿，进而威胁到网络上的自由表达，呼吁人们警惕并抵制这种审查行为。最后，文章指出解决这一问题需要政治上的努力，而非单纯的技术手段。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：支付处理平台对某些行业的限制及由此引发的更广泛的讨论，包括 censorship（审查）、支付基础设施的公平性以及可能的替代方案。

不同观点：
• [whatamidoingyo] 讲述了自己建立约会网站的经历，尽管符合Stripe的条款（不允许成人内容），但账户仍被关闭。他尝试寻找其他支付处理方案，如CCBill，但高昂的设置费用让他却步。最终，他不得不放弃这个项目。他指出，自己在规则内操作，但仍受到不公平对待。

• [xfeeefeee] 表达了对这种问题的担忧，虽然自己作为创作者并没有直接面对支付处理的问题，但类似的问题在托管和捐款方面也存在。他提到自己将创作视为一种创意出口，而不依赖于商业化，因此受影响较小，但对其他需要处理支付的人表示同情。

• [pluto_modadic] 建议使用比特币，并引用了一句话强调许多技术问题的背后其实是政治问题。

• [jjcob] 提到类似的问题不仅限于线上支付，也包括银行业对性工作者的歧视性政策，认为这是不合理的。

• [VegaKH] 虽然同意原帖的观点，但对原帖的写作方式和逻辑提出批评，认为作者没有形成有效的论证，且有自我推销的嫌疑。他强调，两家美国公司不应掌控全球的道德审查标准，应该更多关注权力滥用的问题。

• [jacknews] 认为支付处理应被视为公共基础设施，应该为所有合法行为提供服务，类似水电等公用事业。

• [dedicate] 指出，关注成人内容被审查的问题只是表面现象，更严重的是这种权力可能延伸到政治捐款或新闻网站等其他领域，将过多的控制权交给少数公司高管。

• [linotype] 虽然不太情愿，但承认加密货币可能是这种情况下的有效解决方案，因为传统公司过于懦弱，不敢对抗审查。

• [boopmaster] 提供了一个资源链接，声称可以帮助应对这种问题。

• [busterarm] 提到在日本，Suica等支付系统尚未扩展到在线购物领域，表示对此感到意外。

• [OutOfHere] 认为当前加密货币已经足够多样化和普及，应该可以解决支付处理受限的问题，并建议使用Monero以增强隐私保护。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于支付处理公司是否有权基于自己的道德标准关闭账户，以及这种权力是否应该受到更多监管。
• 讨论还涉及到更广泛的审查问题，包括未来可能影响政治捐款或新闻网站的情况。
• 加密货币被多次提及，作为可能的替代解决方案，但也有评论对其可行性持保留态度。
• 部分评论对原帖的写作方式和逻辑提出批评，认为讨论偏离了核心问题。

总结：讨论围绕支付处理平台的限制展开，涉及审查、公平性及替代方案等问题，其中加密货币被多次提及作为可能的解决方案，但也存在争议。

44679406.article_content:
This is a furry blog, where I write about whatever interests me and sign it with my fursona’s name. I sometimes talk about furry fandom topics, but I sometimes also talk about applied cryptography.
If you got a mild bit of emotional whiplash from that sentence, the best list of posts to start reading to get a feel for my usual fare is
here
.
When one of my more technical blog posts makes it to Hacker News or Reddit, I will inevitably read some pearl-clutching comment declaring the inclusion of furry art on my furry blog as somehow “pornographic” (
as absurd as that really is
).
Considering the recent action taken
against games with NSFW content on Steam and itch.io
, it’s high time we really talked about the threat of payment processors being weaponized against free expression online.
How We Got Here
The weaponization of payment processors to enact target censorship is not a new tactic. It was famously
used by the US government against Wikileaks in 2010
, and more recently
against SciHub
(for daring to make academic papers freely available online).
This is a problem that technologists have been
acutely
aware of for decades.
Separately, organizations like
Collective Shout
(the one behind the recent Steam and itch.io censorship waves) and
Exodus Cry
(who went
after Pornhub
) have adopted the tactic of targeting payment processors to enforce their weird brand of Christianity onto the rest of us.
On Queerphobia in “Christian Activism”
While researching this topic, I came across many Internet comments that claimed that Collective Shout has anti-LGBTQ motives. However,
I could not find any evidence to substantiate this claim
.
Art:
CMYKat
It’s not necessarily true that every Christian activist movement is bigoted. However, this relationship exists with sufficient frequency (
even if they try to obfuscate it
) that we would be remiss not to at least be
cautious
.
Exodus Cry, in particular, has
well-known anti-LGBTQ+ roots
, with its founder campaigning against gay marriage.
Collective Shout is certainly following the Exodus Cry playbook for censoring adult content online, yet also claims to be a “feminist” organization (where Exodus Cry merely calls itself a Christian one).
Interestingly, Collective Shout’s founder, Melinda Tankard Reist, is famously
opposed to women’s right to body autonomy
. This is generally an anti-feminist position to take, and is enough to raise eyebrows about the organization’s actual motives.
But I must emphasize: There is no specific evidence to date that Collective Shout (or Melinda in particular) holds any specific anti-LGBTQ views. Melinda has
previously threatened to sue bloggers
for allegedly misrepresenting her viewpoint before, so being careless with these assertions is not a good idea.
All that said, anti-abortion politics and opposition to LGBT rights often share a bed. If someone uncovers proof of their stance either way, I will update this section at a later date.
But for now, it remains to be seen. I urge people to not spread unsubstantiated claims online. Misinformation doesn’t help you.
Why Oppose Collective Shout?
If you read into the
specific
types of pornographic content that were being targeted by Collective Shout, it’s quite harrowing.
At the top of the list was an incest rape game called
No Mercy
, which has separately
sparked outrage for glorifying sexual abuse
. This is disgusting stuff, and will make many people sympathetic to its removal. I personally won’t lose any sleep over finding out that glorifying rape isn’t profitable.
The problem, however, is
how
Collective Shout achieved its goals.
They didn’t succeed through a petition to Steam, or to one of the governments that have jurisdiction over Steam and/or the developer of this game.
They pressured the payment processors into demanding Steam and itch.io comply with the activists’ demands. The term of art for this extralegal tactic is
“jawboning”
.
Neither Visa nor Mastercard are elected by the people, yet they have unchecked power to decide who can engage in commerce on the Internet.
This is a vulnerability that will be exploited by other groups unless we close it.
Even if we are ultra-charitable and assume that Collective Shout will never try to scrub LGBTQIA+ content from the Internet, what’s to stop another “Christian” anti-queer organization from learning from their victory and increasing the pressure?
What’s to stop someone from using the same exact tactic to censor my blog for *checks notes* being perceived by Hacker News users as “pornographic” just because I’m a furry?
Art:
AJ
To right-wing extremists that don the cloak of Christianity for their bigotry, such at the Heritage Foundation, any visible queerness is framed as pornographic, and therefore must be purged for the sake of “the children.”
What Can We Do?
This is a political problem, not a technical one.
Repeat after me: all technical problems of sufficient scope or impact are actually political problems first.
Eleanor Saitta

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI工具（如Kiro、Claude Code、Sketch.dev等）在软件开发中的应用和效果的讨论，包括实际使用体验、工具对比以及对开发流程的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持并推荐使用AI工具**：
   - **agrippanux**：分享了自己使用Claude Code和其新推出的Agents工具的积极体验，认为这些工具帮助他更高效地完成了开发任务，并提高了代码质量。他还提到使用多个代理（agents）进行计划和反馈循环，最终在短时间内完成了需要两天才能完成的工作。
   - **sqrtc**：同样分享了使用Kiro解决复杂问题的成功经验，强调工具帮助他更清晰地思考问题，并逐步解决了问题。
   - **glietu**：认为基于规格说明的开发对于没有编码背景的人来说是一个重大改变，使得他们能够参与到项目中，并整合开源工具。

• **对AI工具的**质疑和批评**：
   - **hansmayer**：质疑文章的真实性，认为作者没有分享自己使用AI工具的真实体验，而是依赖机器生成的内容，质疑人类是否还需要通过语言表达自己的思想。
   - **lvl155**：认为Kiro并没有带来新的价值，指出这种工作流早已存在，并批评Kiro花时间制作宣传视频而不是增加实用功能。
   - **Cu3PO42**：使用Kiro生成了过多的代码，虽然功能正常，但解决方案过于复杂，需要手动优化。

• **工具对比与成本讨论**：
   - **jeffrallen**：提到自己使用Sketch.dev，认为其比Kiro需要更少的监督，并且具备自我评估的功能，整体体验更好。
   - **999900000999**：指出Kiro的主要优势是亚马逊支付LLM的使用费用，而其他工具如Claude Code和Vs Code的Agent模式则需要自己付费。讨论了LLM成本降低的必要性，并预测未来会有人找到运行顶级LLM模型的廉价方法。

data.title: Show HN: Apple Health MCP Server
data.author: _neil
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为 **Apple Health MCP Server** 的项目，它允许用户通过自然语言和SQL查询Apple Health数据。该项目使用DuckDB进行高效的数据分析，目前依赖于Eric Wolter的**Simple Health Export CSV**应用来导出Apple Health数据为CSV格式。主要功能包括自然语言查询、SQL查询执行、自动生成健康报告、高效数据加载和智能缓存。用户可以通过npx直接使用该项目，并需要设置环境变量如`HEALTH_DATA_DIR`来指定CSV文件目录。项目提供了多种工具如`health_schema`、`health_query`和`health_report`来帮助分析和查询健康数据。开发者可以克隆项目并按照说明进行本地开发，同时也欢迎贡献代码，但需遵循项目规范。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何处理和分析Apple Health数据，特别是数据导出、安全性和应用场景

不同观点：
• tosh提供了一个将Apple Health导出的XML文件转换为时序数据（.parquet）的工具，并可以导入clickhouse或duckdb。
• woodylondon赞赏该工具，但也提到自己通过CSV和云数据库处理健康数据，关注数据安全问题，并指出个人定制化仪表盘的需求。
• leguy对工具表示赞赏，并询问是否可以提出任意问题，特别是关于LLM生成查询的未来应用。
• hcm推荐了另一个将Apple Health数据导入duckdb的工具，并提供了相关链接。
• friggeri提到自己正在开发一个AI跑步教练应用，并希望交流如何有效利用AI分析锻炼和制定计划。
• monatron分享了自己类似的项目，使用Auto Export将健康数据导出到SQLite数据库，并计划构建一个健康/健身代理。
• hahahacorn开玩笑地提到该工具在开发中的潜在用途，比如通过RubyLLM进行健康指标分析。
• felixrieseberg表示如果将该工具打包为桌面扩展，愿意将其添加到Claude的目录中。
• voska介绍了他们为解决类似问题而构建的平台sensai.fit。
• formerly_proven指出Apple Health原生导出功能生成的XML文件过大，但可以通过Shortcut导出特定数据点到CSV。
• brandonb提到iPhone和Apple Watch生成的生物标记数据丰富，但解释能力有限，表示愿意合作改进工具。
• beaker52希望代理能够更新血压和体重等数据。
• solarkraft表达了对Screen Time数据未包含在Apple Health中的不满。
• vincvinc询问是否有推动Apple使数据互兼容的倡议或法律。

补充讨论：
• 数据安全和隐私是用户关注的一个重要问题，尤其是在涉及健康数据时。
• 不同用户对工具的功能有不同需求，例如数据导入/导出、AI分析、定制化仪表盘等。
• 争议的焦点之一是Apple Health数据导出的格式和大小问题，以及如何更便捷地处理和分析这些数据。
• 有用户关注是否可以通过LLM生成查询来分析健康数据，以及如何更有效地与现有系统集成。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于推动数据互兼容的倡议或法律，反映了用户对数据可移植性和互操作性的需求。

Apple Health MCP Server
An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for querying Apple Health data using SQL. Built with DuckDB for fast, efficient health data analysis.
Note
This project currently relies on the
Simple Health Export CSV
app by
Eric Wolter
. See
Exporting Data
below for more info on how best to use the app.
This is currently the easiest way I could find to quickly and reliably get Apple Health data exported in CSV format. If you have ideas of better ways to import data, please submit an issue.
Features
Natural language querying
: Your MCP client translates your questions to database queries
SQL Query Execution
: Direct SQL queries against your Apple Health data
Automated Reports
: Generate weekly/monthly health summaries
Efficient Data Loading
: Lazy loading with configurable time windows
Smart Caching
: Query result caching with TTL
Installation
No installation required! Use directly with npx via Claude Desktop or other MCP clients.
Usage with Claude Desktop
Add to your Claude Desktop configuration (
~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
):
{
"mcpServers"
: {
"apple-health"
: {
"command"
:
"
npx
"
,
"args"
: [
"
@neiltron/apple-health-mcp
"
],
"env"
: {
"HEALTH_DATA_DIR"
:
"
/path/to/your/health/export
"
}
}
}
}
Environment Variables
HEALTH_DATA_DIR
(required): Path to your Apple Health CSV export directory
MAX_MEMORY_MB
(optional): Maximum memory usage in MB (default: 1024)
CACHE_SIZE
(optional): Number of cached query results (default: 100)
Example Configuration
{
"mcpServers"
: {
"apple-health"
: {
"command"
:
"
npx
"
,
"args"
: [
"
@neiltron/apple-health-mcp
"
],
"env"
: {
"HEALTH_DATA_DIR"
:
"
/Users/yourname/Downloads/HealthAll_2025-07-202_01-04-39_SimpleHealthExportCSV
"
,
"MAX_MEMORY_MB"
:
"
2048
"
}
}
}
}
Exporting Data
To use get your data:
Download the
Simple Health Export CSV
app for iOS.
Tap the
All
button in the app to download all data for your desired time range (default 1 month).
When prompted, Airdrop it to your computer or transfer it some other way.
Unzip the file to your desired location
Set the
HEALTH_DATA_DIR
value in your MCP config. See
Example Configuration
above.
Available Tools
health_schema
: Get information about available tables and their structure
health_query
: Execute SQL queries directly on your health data
health_report
: Generate comprehensive health reports
Data Structure
The server expects Apple Health data exported as CSV files with the following naming pattern:
HKQuantityTypeIdentifier*.csv
- Quantitative health metrics
HKCategoryTypeIdentifier*.csv
- Categorical health data
HKWorkoutActivityType*.csv
- Workout and activity data
Each CSV file should have these columns:
type
: The specific health metric type
sourceName
: Source device/app
startDate
: Start timestamp (UTC)
endDate
: End timestamp (UTC)
value
: The measurement value
unit
: Unit of measurement
Development
For local development:
#
Clone and install dependencies
git clone https://github.com/neiltron/apple-health-mcp.git
cd
apple-health-mcp
npm install
#
Build the project
npm run build
#
Type checking
npm run typecheck
Troubleshooting
Common Issues
"No data found"
: Check that your CSV files are in the correct directory
Memory errors
: Reduce
MAX_MEMORY_MB
or use shorter time windows
Slow queries
: Ensure you're filtering by date ranges
Missing tables
: Table names are lowercase (e.g.,
hkquantitytypeidentifierheartrate
)
Contributing
Contributions are welcome! Please ensure:
Code follows existing patterns
TypeScript types are properly defined
Error handling is comprehensive
Performance impact is considered
License
MIT

主要讨论点：关于巴西Pix支付系统与其他国家支付系统（如美国FedNow和印度UPI）的比较，及其对传统信用卡公司（如Visa和Mastercard）的影响。

不同观点：
• **Pix的优越性及对信用卡的影响**：
  - **ojosilva**认为Pix是目前最好的即时支付平台之一，能够与印度的UPI媲美，且在采用率上高于西方国家。Pix让商家和消费者都更喜欢使用，而信用卡则带有隐性成本（如利息和手续费）。
  - **zanellato19**补充说，Pix将帮助巴西人摆脱信用卡的高利率压榨，带来经济自由。

• **技术与国际对比**：
  - **andrewjl**询问Pix与即将推出的美国FedNow在技术上有何不同，特别提到了Pix即将推出的分期付款功能。
  - **diego_moita**认为Pix、印度UPI和肯尼亚Mpesa等支付系统正在催生新型货币形式，这些系统不仅会削弱Visa和Mastercard的影响力，还会挑战PayPal、Apple Pay和Google Pay等平台，并预测未来将出现多种国际支付货币竞争的局面。

• **政治与国际反应**：
  - **Argonaut998**提到特朗普对Pix及巴西的指责，认为这是对Mastercard和Visa的歧视，同时也指出了Visa和Mastercard在全球的垄断地位，特别是在巴西的"parcelas"（分期付款）系统中的主导作用。
  - **atbpaca**指出，特朗普对Pix的攻击实际上可能是在全球范围内推广Pix，因为这种曝光让更多国家注意到了Pix。

• **经济与区域差异**：
  - **anonymousDan**关注Visa和Mastercard在巴西的高额交易抽成对巴西经济的影响，认为减少这些公司对经济的控制对巴西是有利的。
  - **cynicalpeace**对拉丁美洲国家普遍采用的分期付款（cuotas）系统表示困惑，因为在高利率国家这种现象很普遍，而在美国却几乎没有。

补充讨论：
• **Pix的未来发展**：
  - **cadamsdotcom**认为Pix目前的成功值得祝贺，但真正的胜利是在未来10年内继续满足巴西人的需求。
  
• **安全与技术问题**：
  - **vitorgrs**提到Google Pay已支持Pix，但Apple Pay尚未实施，显示出不同科技公司在采用Pix上的态度差异。
  
• **个人安全建议**：
  - **childintime**提出了一种个人安全措施：旅行者应设置两个PIN码，其中一个用于紧急情况（如被胁迫时）以限制交易金额。

争议焦点：
• **Visa和Mastercard的垄断与反制**：

Highlights
Over the past three months, we have continued to scale the
thinking capability
of Qwen3-235B-A22B, improving both the
quality and depth
of reasoning. We are pleased to introduce
Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507
, featuring the following key enhancements:
Significantly improved performance
on reasoning tasks, including logical reasoning, mathematics, science, coding, and academic benchmarks that typically require human expertise — achieving
state-of-the-art results among open-source thinking models
.
Markedly better general capabilities
, such as instruction following, tool usage, text generation, and alignment with human preferences.
Enhanced 256K long-context understanding
capabilities.

data.title: Programming vehicles in games
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了在游戏中编程车辆的核心原则，特别是在不同游戏中如何实现车辆的驾驶体验。文章指出，游戏并不是纯粹的物理模拟，而是通过操控现实来传递特定体验。车辆游戏可以从卡通化的《马里奥赛车》到高度写实的《iRacing》各不相同，因为玩家对“高速驾驶”的期望往往来自电影、游戏等二手经验，而非直接的现实体验。因此，编程车辆时，关键不在于完全模拟真实物理，而在于传达预期的驾驶感受。文章还分享了作者在开发游戏《AV-Racer》时的迭代过程，从简单的牛顿模型开始，通过不断调整和优化，尝试实现更真实的驾驶体验。最终，作者认识到实现车辆模拟的挑战在于平衡“体验”和“机器”两个复杂领域。

Programming Vehicles in Games
The fundamental principles needed to get a functional vehicle in your game.
From my talk at the
Better Software Conference
on July the 13th, 2025.
est. reading time: 45 minutes
Watch the video of the talk here:
Table of Contents
The special case of cars
Chasing the Feel: The Iterative Path to AV-Racer
A Conceptual Model of Vehicle Simulation
The Engine
The Gearbox
Implementing the engine and drivetrain: From Curve to Code
The engine's equation
The driven wheel's equation
The Tire Model
Longitudinal Tire Forces
The Slip Ratio
Lateral Tire Forces
The Slip Angle
Combining the longitudinal and lateral components
The Friction Circle
From a driver's point of view
Integration onto the chassis
Cars are everywhere in games. They're a staple element of many genres, even in games that aren't strictly about cars. If a game world involves any sort of traversal, chances are there's a vehicle in it (unless you're deep in the realm of fantasy where you are riding a horse. The following will not cover programming horses, I apologize).
The special case of cars
The range of experiences that games offer through vehicles is massive. And that's what makes them fascinating to work with. Ever since I was a kid, I've played a variety of racing and vehicle games. I'd always chase the next racing title as soon as it hit the platform I had. But what struck me over time wasn't just the excitement of new cars or tracks; it was how different each experience felt, even though they all had cars at their core.
And here's the key insight: games are not physics engines. They are experiences. And racing games, more than many others, deliberately manipulate reality to deliver those experiences. With shooting games, for example, we expect certain behavior; bullets flying in straight lines, recoil, reloads. If those expectations aren't met, the game feels “off.” But with vehicles? There's an incredible amount of wiggle room.
Take Mario Kart. It's about as far from realistic driving as you can get; you're drifting on sand, tossing shells at your friends, and racing in a mushroom-powered go-kart that's all squashed proportions and cartoon physics. And yet it's beloved. It sells the fantasy of driving.
On the opposite end, you have full-blown simulators like iRacing or Assetto Corsa. Here, the experience is carefully crafted to reflect the nuance and challenge of real-life motorsport. People sink thousands of dollars into rigs just to replicate the feeling of being behind the wheel. And yet; both these games are programming cars at their core. They just prioritize different aspects of that experience.
So why the variability? Why can games get away with such a broad spectrum of driving models?
It's because when it comes to cars, we derive our expectations of them not just from first hand experience. Our understanding of what “driving fast” feels like is often built from second-hand sources; films, games, pop culture. We've all seen the hero of a movie shift gears a dozen times in a straight-line drag race. It's absurd, has nothing to do with reality, but it communicates something. It sells the feeling of acceleration, intensity, control. So kids get it; they want to “shift up” because it feels like doing something meaningful. It's the visceral feeling of controling something large and heavy at break-neck speeds.
So the key question for anyone implementing vehicles in a game isn't “what are the real physics I need to simulate?”, it's “what experience do I want to convey?”. From there you get to the question of “how do I implement that?”.
I've come to realize that the challenge of simulating vehicles in games lies in bridging two complex worlds: the experience and the machine. You need to understand both. Only then can you decide how and where to bend the rules; because game design isn't about simulating reality, it's about shaping it to fit your vision.
Chasing the Feel: The Iterative Path to AV-Racer
My first attempt at simulating a vehicle in a game was AV Racer, and it began as a simple top-down sprite using a basic Newtonian model. I controlled the car's movement with acceleration and braking, tied angular velocity to speed (so it wouldn't rotate on the spot), and called it a day.
Did it look like a car? Sort of. Did it feel like one? Not at all. It was more like a robotic puck skating around on invisible rails. So, iterating on that, I started hacking in some nonlinear curves and smoothing functions to mimic a behavior of a sliding car, trying to push away from the rigid feel. I faked the trail, exaggerated the drift, tweaked the angular momentum. It was all hacks, but it worked, somewhat. At least until Casey Muratori tried it and pointed out it looked like a car on ice, a spaceship. And he was right. It floated rather than gripped.
So I went back to the drawing board, already sunk in the hacky method, I added more magical numbers, created a para

data.title: Dwl: Dwm for Wayland
data.author: theycallhermax
data.article_summary: **dwl** 是一个为 Wayland 设计的轻量级可定制合成器（compositor），基于 **wlroots** 库，旨在提供与 **dwm** 在 X11 中类似的功能和设计理念。其特点包括易于理解和扩展，通过 **config.h** 进行配置，且尽量减少外部依赖。要构建 **dwl**，需要依赖 **libinput**、**wayland**、**wlroots** 等库，并可通过编辑 **config.h** 进行配置，配置后需重新编译才能生效。此外，它支持 **XWayland** 以兼容 X11 程序，但需手动启用。用户可以通过加入社区分享自定义补丁。运行 **dwl** 时，它支持多种后端，可以直接从控制台或 Wayland/X11 会话中启动。

主要讨论点：用户对基于Wayland的窗口管理器及其与dwm关系的看法和体验

不同观点：
• exiguus：作为dwm的长期用户，由于dwm不支持Wayland，他转向了sway，并将sway视为dwm的继任者。他还提到曾经关注过dwl，但如今重新审视它。
• xwiz：推荐了自己常用的窗口管理器Niri，展示了对TWM的偏好，未直接评论Wayland相关项目。
• jauntywundrkind：对该项目表示赞赏，认为在wlroots和新的场景图API基础上构建一个好的Wayland实现已不再困难。
• gundamdoubleO：长期使用dwm，因dwl的存在而顺利切换到Wayland，认为切换过程几乎无痛。
• alex-moon：虽然喜欢dwm，但认为它不够成熟，最终选择了Hyprland，并认为Hyprland有许多改进。
• cnity：提出是否可以将此项目作为dwm的补丁提交，暗示可能希望dwm官方接纳类似功能。
• dannyobrien：分享了一个带有Guile Scheme支持的dwl fork链接，提供了额外的选择。

• dodomodo：仅有[flagged]标记，未提供实质性评论。

争议焦点：
• 不同用户对dwm及dwl等Wayland替代品的成熟度和功能有不同看法，例如aexiguus和gundamdoubleO对dwl的积极体验与alex-moon对dwm成熟度的质疑。
• cnity提出的dwm补丁建议引发了关于dwm项目发展方向的讨论。

README.md
dwl - dwm for Wayland
Join us on our IRC channel:
#dwl on Libera Chat
Or on the community-maintained
Discord server
.
dwl is a compact, hackable compositor for
Wayland
based on
wlroots
. It is
intended to fill the same space in the Wayland world that dwm does in X11,
primarily in terms of functionality, and secondarily in terms of
philosophy. Like dwm, dwl is:
Easy to understand, hack on, and extend with patches
One C source file (or a very small number) configurable via
config.h
Tied to as few external dependencies as possible
Getting Started:
Latest semi-stable
release
This is probably where you want to start. This builds against the
wlroots
versions currently shipping in major distributions. If your
distribution's
wlroots
version is older, use an earlier dwl
release
.
The
wlroots
version against which a given
dwl
release builds is specified
with each release on the
release
page
Development branch
main
Active development progresses on the
main
branch. The
main
branch is built
against a late (and often changing) git commit of wlroots. While the adventurous
are welcome to use
main
, it is a rocky road. Using
main
requires that the
user be willing to chase git commits of wlroots. Testing development pull
requests may involve merging unmerged pull requests in
wlroots
' git repository
and/or git commits of wayland.
Building dwl
dwl has the following dependencies:
libinput
wayland
wlroots (compiled with the libinput backend)
xkbcommon
wayland-protocols (compile-time only)
pkg-config (compile-time only)
dwl has the following additional dependencies if XWayland support is enabled:
libxcb
libxcb-wm
wlroots (compiled with X11 support)
Xwayland (runtime only)
Install these (and their
-devel
versions if your distro has separate
development packages) and run
make
. If you wish to build against a released
version of wlroots (
you probably do
), use a
release
or a
0.x branch
. If
you want to use the unstable development
main
branch, you need to use the git
version of
wlroots
.
To enable XWayland, you should uncomment its flags in
config.mk
.
Configuration
All configuration is done by editing
config.h
and recompiling, in the same
manner as dwm. There is no way to separately restart the window manager in
Wayland without restarting the entire display server, so any changes will take
effect the next time dwl is executed.
As in the dwm community, we encourage users to share patches they have
created. Check out the
dwl-patches
repository!
Running dwl
dwl can be run on any of the backends supported by wlroots. This means you can
run it as a separate window inside either an X11 or Wayland session, as well as
directly from a VT console. Depending on your distro's setup, you may need to
add your user to the
video
and
input
groups before you can run dwl on a
VT. If you are using
elogind
or
systemd-logind
you need to install polkit;
otherwise you need to add yourself in the
seat
group and enable/start the
seatd daemon.
When dwl is run with no arguments, it will launch the server and begin handling
any shortcuts configured in
config.h
. There is no status bar or other

44683011.article_summary: **dwl** 是一个为 Wayland 设计的轻量级可定制合成器（compositor），基于 **wlroots** 库，旨在提供与 **dwm** 在 X11 中类似的功能和设计理念。其特点包括易于理解和扩展，通过 **config.h** 进行配置，且尽量减少外部依赖。要构建 **dwl**，需要依赖 **libinput**、**wayland**、**wlroots** 等库，并可通过编辑 **config.h** 进行配置，配置后需重新编译才能生效。此外，它支持 **XWayland** 以兼容 X11 程序，但需手动启用。用户可以通过加入社区分享自定义补丁。运行 **dwl** 时，它支持多种后端，可以直接从控制台或 Wayland/X11 会话中启动。

data.title: Who has the fastest F1 website (2021)
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 本文是关于2021年F1车队网站加载速度的系列评测之三，主要分析Red Bull车队官网的性能。相比2019年，2021年的Red Bull网站显著提速，总加载时间从15.8秒减少到8.6秒。然而，仍存在一些可优化的问题，如由于不必要的内嵌代码导致内容渲染延迟3秒，主图像由于JavaScript实现和优化不足延迟10秒以上，此外还有字体和关键图像的加载延迟。通过优化图像格式（如使用更小体积的AVIF）、精简内嵌代码和改善资源加载策略，网站性能还有进一步提升空间。总体而言，Red Bull网站虽视觉丰富，但仍有改进潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕图片格式选择、网站性能优化以及具体案例的讨论

不同观点：
• firefoxd：通过小游戏让前端团队了解不同图片格式（JPEG、PNG、WebP、SVG）的适用场景，强调了开发者倾向于使用PNG以追求图片清晰度，但可能会导致网站臃肿。同时指出SVG和WebP的潜在滥用问题，如在SVG中嵌入PNG。

• cjbarber：提出"将核心特质融入所有方面"的原则，并以F1赛车为例，强调速度的重要性。该观点认为无论是实体体验（如检票或食品服务）还是网站设计，速度都应作为关键指标，呼应了firefoxd对网站优化的关注。

• defly：分享了一个当前状态的可视化链接，但未深入展开讨论。

• zaking17：提到《Websites that Suck》一书，指出自己从批判性案例中学习网页设计，并一直致力于创建不糟糕的网站。此评论更偏向设计批判和学习方法。

• snug：在无聊时创建了一个关于当前F1车队的网站链接，似乎是为了展示自己的项目，未深入讨论图片格式问题。

• goshx：表示正在观看比利时冲刺排位赛，并对2025年的版本表示期待，未深入讨论技术问题。

• hhmc：质疑该帖子已有四年历史，询问是否有网站根据反馈进行了改进，关注的是讨论的实际影响和后续行动。

• GaggiX：详细讨论了WebP格式在色彩表现上的缺陷，指出其无法关闭子采样，并推荐使用AVIF格式，认为AVIF得到了所有主流浏览器的支持，是更好的选择。此评论提供了技术细节和替代方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：WebP格式的优劣。GaggiX指出了WebP的色彩问题，而firefoxd则提到WebP和其他格式一样容易被滥用。
• 实际应用：讨论中涉及到多个实际案例和项目链接（如snug的F1网站），但多数未深入展开技术细节。
• 历史反馈：hhmc提出的关于反馈落实的问题，显示出对实际应用效果的关注。

整体来看，讨论围绕图片格式选择、格式特性及其实际应用展开，不同参与者提供了各自的见解和经验。

44682932.article_content:
Who has the fastest F1 website in 2021? Part 3
Posted 29 March 2021
I once spent an hour creating an
F1 lights-out reaction test
which went viral and was even
played by F1 drivers
. That sounds like a brag, and it kinda is, but now whenever I pour days or even weeks of work into something, it just seems so inefficient compared to that time I spent
an hour
on something that went big. Wait! You're not my therapist! Let's look at another F1 website…
This is part 3 in a multi-part series looking at the loading performance of F1 websites. Not interested in F1? It shouldn't matter. This is just a performance review of 10 recently-built/updated sites that have broadly the same goal, but are built by different teams, and have different performance issues.
Part 1: Methodology & Alpha Tauri
Part 2: Alfa Romeo
➡️ Part 3: Red Bull
Part 4: Williams
Part 5: Aston Martin
Part 6: Ferrari
Part 7: Haas
Part 8: McLaren
Bonus: Google I/O
…more coming soon…
Red Bull
Link
Red Bull Racing Honda
First run
6.7s (
raw results
)
Second run
1.9s (
raw results
)
Total
8.6s
2019 total
15.8s (2021 site is 7.2s faster)
Now we're talking! This is a graphically rich, engaging site, and the performance is pretty good! In fact, it's significantly faster than its 2019 site. But there's still room for improvement.
Possible improvements
3 second delay to content-render
caused by unnecessary inlining. Covered in detail below.
10 second delay to main image
caused by a JavaScript responsive images implementation,
like we saw in part 2
. These should be
real responsive images
.
Additional 2 second delay to main image
caused by an extra connection. This problem is
covered in part 1
, but the solution here is just to move the images to the same server as the page.
Additional 2 second delay to main image
caused by poor optimisation. Covered in detail below.
40 second delay to key image
caused by loading it with JavaScript. Covered in detail below.
Additional 30 second delay to that image
caused by poor optimisation. Covered in detail below.
2 second delay to fonts
caused by extra connection. Again, this is
covered in part 1
, but the solution here is just to move the fonts to the same server.
40+ second delay to content-blocking cookie modal
caused by… a number of things,
covered in part 1
.
Remember these delays overlap in some cases.
Issue: Unnecessary inlining
Here's the first bit of the timeline:
The page renders around the 6s mark, which is while the HTML is still downloading. Browsers can stream HTML and render it while it's downloading; it's a great feature of parsed-HTML that many sites don't get the benefit of due to blocking resources. Because the page renders with that one resource, we know there are
no
blocking resources. This suggests the CSS is inlined, and from looking at the source, yep, it is.
Inlining avoids request/response overhead, which is great for render-blocking resources. But also, since it's part of the
page
, you can tailor the inlining for
that page
.
However, that doesn't seem to be what's happening here. Here's what I see in
Chrome DevTools' coverage panel
:
The code in the page is 79.5% unused, which amounts to over 600kB. Compare this to the coverage on
Squoosh
:
…where we used inline content just for the CSS and script needed for the first interaction. The first row there is a non-blocking resource, where coverage doesn't matter so much, but the bottom row is the page, where only 7kB is unused. You can also click on these lines which takes you to a code view of used and unused code:
Anyway, we aren't here to talk about Squoosh. Around three seconds could be shaved off time-to-content on the Red Bull site by making the inlined code tailored to what the page needs for that content-render. The rest can be loaded via external resources.
Issue: Large primary image
Original WebP (99.1 kB)
Optimised WebP (24.8 kB)
AVIF (13.9 kB)
It's great to see them using WebP, but the quality is just set too high. Yes, some detail is lost in the compressed versions, but remember this image has text over the top, and another image over the top.
Actually, let's talk about that image…
Issue: Large overlay image
Original WebP (1.1 MB)
Optimised WebP (620 kB)
AVIF (132 kB)
AVIF for mobile (47.8 kB)
This image sits over the top of the main carousel, and it's a great part of the design. Again, they're using WebP, but maybe not with the right settings. But even with optimised settings, the WebP is still big.
When WebP was created, they designed the alpha channel around things like logos, and things cut-out of photos. In these cases the alpha channel is dominated by large areas of the same value:
Full image
Alpha channel
Because of this, they used the WebP
lossless
mode for the alpha channel, even if the colour data is using the lossy mode. This works well in general, except in cases like this:
Full image
Alpha channel
…where the alpha channel is frequently changing. This is something a lossy codec handles much better. AVIF can perform lossy encodi

data.title: Meta to stop running political ads on Facebook and Instagram in the EU
data.author: aquir
data.article_summary: Meta宣布将从10月起停止在欧盟投放政治、选举和社会议题广告，以避免遵守即将生效的欧盟透明度法规。该法规要求披露政治广告的资金来源及是否使用个人数据进行定向投放，旨在防止信息操纵和外国干涉选举。Meta称这些新规对广告商和平台造成了过度的复杂性和法律不确定性。此前，谷歌也做出了类似决定。欧盟议员Sandro Gozi批评Meta此举是对透明度和民主责任的逃避，质疑其打击虚假信息的承诺。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta停止政治广告在欧盟的影响及相关问题

不同观点：
• [poisonborz] 指出匈牙利政府是欧盟内Meta政治广告的最大支出者，担忧其影响，特别是与德国或欧盟议会相比的显著支出。
• [ajdude] 认为即使屏蔽了政治广告，Facebook上仍有许多非广告的政治内容通过病毒式传播，屏蔽功能效果有限。
• [isodev] 支持政治广告不该存在，认为这是好消息。
• [CommenterPerson] 赞同此举，认为欧盟正在通过一些好的法规来应对互联网的恶化问题。
• [game_the0ry] 感叹社交网络对当今世界的影响，从其创始人的背景联想到当前局势。
• [blitzar] 认为Meta停止政治广告没有损失任何有价值的东西，甚至其股价也未受影响。
• [seydor] 指出欧盟委员会和议会本身就是Facebook上最大的广告商之一，质疑这些是否算作政治广告。
• [Yoric] 简单表达对此消息的积极态度，认为是最好的消息。
• [jabjq] 认为最成功的政治广告通常不是付费的，而是通过其他方式传播的。
• [progbits] 讽刺Meta律师因监管和政治广告透明度规则而需要额外工作，暗示这些规则的必要性。
• [sam-cop-vimes] 简单表达对Meta停止政治广告的支持，认为是清除糟粕。
• [yostrovs] 提出所有涉及意见或试图改变他人想法的言论都应该透明化，以便听众了解背后的意图。
• [mrtksn] 详细描述了政治广告如何被用于操纵舆论，包括右翼和左翼的例子，以及外国干预选举的问题，认为停止政治广告有助于减少这种操纵。
• [duxup] 提出具体情境，质疑如果候选人因特定政策（如“禁止池塘中的鸭子”）而出名，是否可以通过广告来强化此议题，以影响选民。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于政治广告是否应该存在，以及其对政治舆论和选举的潜在影响。
• 讨论中也提到了非付费政治内容通过社交媒体传播的问题，这可能削弱仅限制政治广告的效果。
• 外国干预和政治宣传的透明度问题也被提及，强调了更广泛的监管需求。
• 最后，一些评论对Meta停止政治广告的实际影响持怀疑态度，认为可能不会带来实质性的改变或损失。

Updated to include a response statement from the regulation's rapporteur.
Social media giant Meta announced today that it will stop running political, electoral or social issue advertising in the EU from October, instead of complying with the bloc's transparency rules for political advertising.
EU-wide rules on the transparency of political advertising come into effect from October, with the aim of curbing information manipulation and foreign interference during elections, according to a Council
announcement
on the agreement last year.
The regulation obliges online publishers of political advertisements to disclose whether an ad is paid for by a political actor to make it easier for citizens to recognise political marketing. It also requires disclosure of whether the ad was targeted using personal data.
Meta is sidestepping all these requirements, per its announcement today, as the company says it will no longer allow political, electoral or social issue ads in the EU. It defines these types of ads in its terms and conditions for different territories. Meta said the change would also apply in other "European territories", including the UK.
The company is blaming its decision to end political ads on the EU's Regulation – claiming it's too restrictive and burdensome for advertisers. "Unfortunately, the TTPA [the political ads transparency regulation] introduces significant additional obligations to our processes and systems that create an untenable level of complexity and legal uncertainty for advertisers and platforms operating in the EU," Meta
wrote
.
It said the move won't change any of its other policies for people in the EU as regards debating politics. Nor will it stop politicians from posting content on its social networks. However political actors would not be able to pay Meta to amplify such content.
Responding to Meta's announcement, liberal lawmaker Sandro Gozi, the rapporteur for the EU's regulation on political advertising, said it "confirms a deep allergy to transparency, data protection and democratic accountability." "They [Meta] pretend to fight disinformation, but in reality they are making money from it," he added.
Last year, Google also
announced
that it would stop serving political ads in the EU before the regulation came into effect. It blamed the law for having an overly broad definition of "political advertisement" for it to be able to comply, hence choosing to stop running such ads across the bloc.
But one question both companies' actions raises is how effective their own – typically automated – ad review systems are at detecting political, electoral or social issue ads and stopping them from being distributed. Any political ads that do slip through would automatically breach the EU's transparency rules given their ad systems do not provide these disclosures.
In Meta's case, this is not the first time it's blamed EU laws for forcing it to change its ad behaviour: the tech giant is currently
facing
Digital Markets Act enforcement over its pay-or-consent advertising model.

44683148.article_summary: Meta宣布将从10月起停止在欧盟投放政治、选举和社会议题广告，以避免遵守即将生效的欧盟透明度法规。该法规要求披露政治广告的资金来源及是否使用个人数据进行定向投放，旨在防止信息操纵和外国干涉选举。Meta称这些新规对广告商和平台造成了过度的复杂性和法律不确定性。此前，谷歌也做出了类似决定。欧盟议员Sandro Gozi批评Meta此举是对透明度和民主责任的逃避，质疑其打击虚假信息的承诺。

data.title: My website is one binary (2022)
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者多年来寻找适合自己的网站框架的经历，尝试了多种工具如Ghost、Hugo、Jekyll等，但都不符合其高标准和独特需求。作者重视可完全理解和维护的系统，偏爱简洁、可读性高和快速反馈的代码，追求乐趣和创意。作者最终放弃了常见静态网站生成器如Hugo，因为这些工具依赖于外部服务、社区和更新，违背了其对可靠性和长期可维护性的追求。作者选择使用纯手写HTML，并在自己控制的服务器上托管网站，实现了极简且无依赖的解决方案，虽然工作流程繁琐，但满足了其对简单性、可靠性和自主维护的需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人网站的生成和托管方案，特别是关于单一二进制方案的可行性、优缺点以及使用场景的讨论。

不同观点：
• [liampulles] 支持使用Go编写单一二进制程序生成静态博客网站，认为这种方法在自定义和Markdown写作之间取得了良好平衡。他提供了一个DSL示例和个人网站链接，展示了具体实现。

• [dang] 提供了相关讨论链接，展示了过去关于“单一二进制网站”的讨论，表明这是一个持续被讨论的话题。

• [paranoidxprod] 提到另一个用户的正在开发的新wiki项目，并猜测该项目是否会采用类似的方法进行网站构建。

• [lelanthran] 质疑单一二进制方案的必要性，认为传统方法（如使用web服务器、PHP等）已经足够，并指出Go方案可能过度工程化。他们提供了PHP实现相同功能的简化代码示例。

• [sha16] 分享了自己从Python的Pelican静态网站生成器转向使用Nextjs构建自定义网站的经历，认为这样可以避免处理复杂的模板引擎。

• [exiguus] 对单一二进制方案的可访问性提出质疑，认为Markdown转换为HTML更易于实现可访问性，并分享了自己使用多种技术构建静态网站的经验。

• [usixk] 对帖子的轻松语气表示赞赏，没有提出技术性意见。

• [indigodaddy] 支持单一二进制方案，认为这样可以保持系统的精简和低依赖性。

• [Twey] 对使用Go语言实现单一二进制方案持怀疑态度，认为使用POSIX兼容的sh脚本或JavaScript bundle可能更合适，并提到Google支持的语言和工具链可能面临被放弃的风险。

• [simpaticoder] 提到redbean.dev作为一个类似理念的项目，暗示这可能是另一种实现方式。

• [daitangio] 建议使用Hugo模板和Isso评论系统，认为可以在很短时间内搭建一个不错的网站，同时提到使用Python Django构建博客的教程。

• [Quitschquat] 提到使用CLOG和save-lisp-and-die进行类似开发。

• [xandrius] 表示对不使用大写字母的写作方式不满，认为这是对读者的不尊重。

• [minroot] 简单提到静态网站的低能耗优势。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于单一二进制方案是否过度工程化及其相较于传统方法的实际优势。
• 可访问性是另一个值得注意的讨论点，特别是如何在自定义网站中确保HTML内容的可访问性。
• 不同技术栈和工具链的选择也是讨论的一个重要方面，各用户根据自己的经验提出了不同的建议和看法。

my website is one binary
my website is one binary
2022-04-06
----------------------------
a.k.a. this one weird trick that inspires me to program creatively
i have struggled for years to figure out a website framework that feels good
to me. i tried all of the classics, including but limited to:
- ghost
- hugo
- jekyll
- sr.ht + tarball
- manual html editing
i have very high and unusual standards, and none of the above felt correct to me.
more importantly, none of the above excited me.
i have uncovered the secret. i have discovered my path. a website that feels good.
but first, the search.
mY vALuES
-------------
i place an extremely high value on systems that i am capable of understanding
and trivially maintaining front-to-back as a single individual. i like human-
friendly code that is optimized for readability, and i like extremely fast
feedback loops. i like fun and cleverness and being cute too.
the first recommendation people always get is "hugo." for those who aren't in
the know, hugo is a "static website generator" - aka, it is a program that takes
templates & markdown as input and compiles HTML that you may deploy wherever you'd
like.
people normally couple a static site generator (SSG) framework with some hosting
platform for an ez-pz pretty reliable & fast blog. or so they say.
one of my core values is maintainability. this is true of most everything that
i own. from my framework laptop to my bicycle, i like to be able to get my hands
dirty when things break down, and i will always prefer tools and platforms that
treat users as capable and curious. i make a lot of unconventional sacrifices
and people think it's weird - but the truth is that i _hate_ maintaining things.
i'm extremely bad at it. but when something of mine breaks, i _need_ to be able
to dig in myself, because god knows i'm not responsible enough to go through the
painfully long feedback loop of having someone else help me. (i am so averse to
this in my personal life that i will simply let my broken things stay broken if
i cannot trivially fix them myself)
hence another core value of mine - reliability. i need the thing to work today,
and i need the thing to work in ten years. i spend a lot of time choosing my
things, and i refuse to depend on anyone else to ensure that they continue to
work. i don't care if your company went under, my car will keep working. i don't
care if you end-of-life'd the product, my laptop takes generic components that i
can insert myself. you get the point.
so, when people say "just build your blog with hugo and host it on github pages
bruh!" i am naturally very skeptical. here are some of the dependencies that
hugo + github pages come with:
- github pages, the service
(it must remain up)
- github pages, the product
(it must remain viable)
- hugo, the project
(it has 1,200 dependencies that require constant updates)
- hugo, the community
(they must document the code)
(i cannot read it all myself)
(i have limited time and interest)
- hugo, the plugin ecosystem
(if you rely on any of their plugins)
- hugo, the binary
(it must compile your HTML in roughly the same way over time)
(it must not break your website between releases)
- github pages, the deployment mechanism
(the ability for github to actually deploy the hugo code)
- golang
(it's pretty clear that golang is here to stay)
it could be argued that you could use a single version of hugo forever - but in
my experience that rarely works out. (i quickly run into a bug, and am forced to
upgrade).
nah, i won't - i tried it, i don't like it. people think that it's simple and
effortless, but it's riddled with dependencies (on people, software, and companies)
and winds up making me feel helpless, like my values are being violated.
it took me a long time to figure out why hugo made me feel uneasy.
(to be clear, i am not attacking hugo _specifically_, this is a problem that i
have with most software)
so, clearly, i needed a system that fit my values
plain old html
------------------
i decided that i would host a website on a machine that i controlled, and
program in plain old HTML, and edit everything by hand using vim.
~ * ~ and so i gave birth to the worst workflow ever used ~ * ~
the first draft of https://j3s.sh was built like this - it is where a lot of my
ideas for the layout came from. the website still looks largely the same -
writing HTML by hand felt a lot like doing intensive labor by hand - like
dishwashing with a hand pump instead of a sink. it forced me into an insane level
of minimalism in order to avoid the pain of having to use the workflow.  i
embedded styling directly into the HTML, made cross-site functions as minimal
as possible, and shied away from much styling.
in a lot of ways, this experience was exactly what i had hoped for. it was
simple, reliable, and maintainable - the HTML i wrote could be reused without
modification, and i felt pretty confident that my site would be around for
awhile. i had no dependencies. but i grew ve

data.title: Google Opal
data.author: babushkaboi
data.article_summary: Google Labs推出了名为Opal的新工具，它允许用户通过自然语言和可视化编辑，无代码创建和分享AI微型应用。Opal可以帮助用户将提示、AI模型和工具链接起来，构建多步骤工作流，并提供编辑功能以调整应用。用户可以利用预设模板快速上手，并将完成的作品通过Google账号分享给他人使用。Opal目前在美国进行公开测试，旨在加速AI创意和应用的原型设计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一个新社区聚会和活动策划应用的构想及其相关技术工具的讨论

不同观点：
• **功能与设计构想**：[basch] 详细描述了一个集活动策划与事件管理于一体的应用构想，包括类似约会应用的界面、项目管理软件的功能以及组织结构图和招聘软件的特点。该用户强调了应用的多功能性，如活动角色的分配、AI辅助策划以及时间线管理等功能。

• **类似工具的提及**：[martypitt] 提到 tldraw 团队之前做过类似的项目，名为 tldraw Computer，并认为该团队在产品个性化方面做得更好。

• **对企业参与的批评**：[dmonitor] 对例子中提到的“制作企业社交媒体帖子”表示不满，认为需要认真讨论如何将企业从人类互联网中移除。

• **趋势与竞争分析**：
  ◦ [Alifatisk] 提问这种类型的应用是否会成为LLM（大语言模型）领域的下一个趋势，并提供了相关登陆页面的链接。
  ◦ [ctxc] 对产品在公测阶段仅在美国发布表示质疑，认为这种做法并不新颖。
  ◦ [klysm] 对Google产品通常很快被关闭表示担忧，预测该新产品可能也会在几个月后被关闭。

• **技术工具对比**：
  ◦ [SomaticPirate] 猜测这是否是Google推出的n8n（一个开源的工作流自动化工具）的竞争对手。
  ◦ [pbronez] 认为“AI代理”实际上是低代码/基于流的编程工具，只是升级了NLP模块。
  ◦ [umeshunni] 提到该应用让他想起了Yahoo Pipes，这是早期的流程化工作流工具。

补充讨论：
• [josefritzishere] 提到期待看到该产品被列入“Killed by Google”（一个记录Google关闭的产品和服务的网站），暗示对Google产品持久性的不信任。

总结：讨论围绕一个新应用的功能设计、类似工具的比较、企业参与的争议以及对Google产品策略的质疑展开。参与者提供了不同的视角，包括产品设计的细节、市场趋势、技术工具对比以及对企业行为的批评。

It’s never been easier to harness the power of AI models, prompts, and tools into working AI applications. We’re excited to announce Opal, a new experimental tool from Google Labs that lets you build and share powerful AI mini apps that chain together prompts, models, and tools — all using simple natural language and visual editing. Opal is a great tool to accelerate prototyping AI ideas and workflows, demonstrate a proof of concept with a functional app, build custom AI apps to boost your productivity at work, and more. We’re launching it today and are so excited to see what you build.
Now available in public beta
Opal is brand new and experimental. We’re launching today in a US-only public beta because we believe the best way to build a new product is with our community, right from the start.
Bring your prompts to life, no code required
Though Opal is an experiment, it’s packed with powerful features designed to make your ideas a reality:
Create workflows
When building software, the sequence of steps a user takes to accomplish a specific goal is called a workflow. Opal helps simplify and visualize these workflows, empowering you to build powerful, multi-step apps by chaining together prompts, AI model calls, and other tools. Just describe the logic, and Opal builds the visual workflow for you.
Make edits
Opal translates your instructions into a visual workflow, giving you fine-grained control without ever needing to see a line of code. You can build and remix your AI mini-apps using conversational natural language commands, a visual editor, or a combination of both. If you want to tweak a step’s prompt, add a new feature, or call a tool, you can edit in the visual editor, or just describe the change.
Share your app
Once your app is ready, you can share it as an app for others to use immediately, using their own Google account.
Link to Youtube Video
(visible only when JS is disabled)
Get started with Opal
To help you get started, Opal features a demo gallery with starter templates. You can use these pre-built AI apps as they are, or remix them to fit your exact needs.
Opal introduces a new way to create with AI. It’s about empowering creators, innovators, and doers to build the tools they imagine by transforming simple prompts into powerful mini apps.
Ready to start building? Welcome to
Opal
.

data.title: Implementing a functional language with graph reduction (2021)
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用Haskell实现一个基于图归约的函数式语言。该实现分为三部分：λ-calculus解析器、λ-calculus到组合逻辑的编译器以及图归约器。首先，通过解析器将λ-calculus和整数解析为简单的表达式。其次，编译器使用括号抽象和优化规则将λ-calculus表达式转换为组合逻辑（S, K, I, B, C, Y）。最后，图归约器将组合逻辑表达式放入图数据结构中，并通过可变的`STRef`引用实现图的原地销毁性归约。本文还展示了如何用Haskell表示λ-表达式和环境，并提供了简单的解析器代码示例。最终，通过SKI组合逻辑的图归约实现了该语言的后端。虽然最初尝试扩展到闭笛卡尔范畴（CCC）失败，但最终成功实现了预期功能。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [tromp] 提到了Ben Lynn在一个IOCCC获奖作品中实现了Haskell的子集，使用图归约引擎进行小型的C程序编译。他还提到Lennart Augustsson实现了更大规模且更适合生产的Haskell到组合子逻辑的编译器，提供了相关资源链接。
• [throwaway81523] 推荐了Simon Peyton Jones（SPJ）关于同一主题的书，暗示该书对理解相关内容非常有帮助，并提供了书籍链接。
• [taliesinb] 从名绑定的角度探讨了图与树之间的关系，并试图寻找单子范畴（monoidal category）相关的形式化理论，特别是将S和K组合子视为类似于复制和删除操作的直觉观察，询问是否存在这种观察的正式版本。

补充讨论：

• 争议焦点似乎在于如何形式化地理解组合子逻辑中的操作与范畴论中的概念之间的联系，尤其是对S和K组合子的观察是否存在更正式的理论支持。
• 不同评论者提供了相关的参考资料和文献链接，为深入理解和进一步研究提供了资源。

44685669.article_content:
Implementing a Functional Language with Graph Reduction
Posted on December 27, 2021
by Thomas Mahler
Abstract
Implementing a small functional language with a classic combinator based graph-reduction machine in Haskell.
The implementation is structured into three parts:
A λ-calculus parser from
A Combinatory Compiler
which was extended to cover a tiny functional language based on the untyped λ-calculus.
A compiler from λ-calculus to combinatory logic combinators (S,K,I,B,C and Y) which is based on bracket-abstraction and some optimization rules.
A graph-reducer. Combinator terms are allocated into a graph data-structure.
Which is then reduced by applying combinator graph-reduction. The destructive inplace reduction of the graph is made possible by using
STRef
mutable references.
Introduction
In my
last blog post
I presented two ways of transforming λ-terms into variable free representations:
- bracket abstraction to combinatory logic terms (SKI) and
- bracket abstraction to terms of closed cartesian categories (CCC).
I demonstrated that both representations are equivalent as they imply the same reduction rules.
My original intention was to extend an existing Haskell CCC implementation to a proof-of-concept implementation of a small functional language. I even promised to cover this in my next blog post.
I invested a lot of time in this idea but I failed to get it off the ground.
At least the code of these experiments has been preserved
.
So I came back to writing a SKI graph-reduction as the backend of my language implementation. This is a well-worn path. I took the basic ideas from the classic
compiling functional languages
which dates back to 1988.
Fortunately, I did not fail this time!
In the following I’m explaining my implementation approach. I’ll also share some of my insights and talk about possible future extensions.
representing λ-expressions
I’m aiming at a very rudimentary language that is basically just pure λ-calculus plus integers. Here is an example:
Y
=
λf
.
(λx
.
x x)(λx
.
f(x x))
fact
=
Y
(\f n
->
if
(is0 n)
1
(
*
n (f (sub1 n))))
main
=
fact
10
As you can see it’s possible to use classical λ-calculus notation
λx . x x
as well as Haskell syntax:
\x -> x x
. It’s also possible to freely mix both styles.
λ-expressions can be assigned to names in a top-level environment by using the
=
sign. those names may be referred to in other λ-expressions.
As of now recursive (also mutually recursive) references are not supported.
The
main
expression has a special meaning; it is interpreted as the entry point to a program.
With this knowledge at hand you will immediately recognize that the above program will compute the factorial of 10. Where
fact
is defined in a non-recursive way by means of the fixed-point combinator
Y
.
Expressions of this language are represented by the data type
Expr
:
infixl
5
:@
data
Expr
=
Expr
:@
Expr
|
Var
String
|
Int
Integer
|
Lam
String
Expr
deriving
(
Eq
,
Show
)
The top-level environment which maps names to λ-Expressions is represented by the following type:
type
Environment
=
[(
String
,
Expr
)]
The Parser
There is not much to see in
this area
. It’s just a simple Parsec based parser. Most of the code was taken from
A Combinatory Compiler
. I just added the parsing of Integers.
The parser module exports to function
parseEnvironmentEither
and
parseEnvironment
. The former is a total function returning an Either:
parseEnvironmentEither :: String -> Either ParseError Environment
, whereas the latter simply returns an
Environment
but may throw run-time errors.
The following
snippet
demonstrates how a program is parsed into an Environment:
testSource ::
String
testSource
=
"Y    = λf -> (λx -> x x)(λx -> f(x x)) \n"
++
"fact = Y(λf n -> if (is0 n) 1 (* n (f (sub1 n)))) \n"
++
"main = fact 10 \n"
main
=
do
let
env
=
parseEnvironment testSource
mapM_
print
env
putStrLn
""

Bracket abstraction
Motivation
Of course it is possible to write interpreters that evaluate these λ-expression to normalform.
This is what any Lisp or Scheme eval/apply interpreter does at its core
(See a tiny example here)
.
One of the most problematic areas of these interpreters is the handling of variables. In order to provide static binding you will need closures that captures the current environment of variable bindings and thread them through the whole interpreter execution.
Language implemetors have thus experimented with many ways to tackle this issue. One of the most influential ideas was to completely get rid of variables by abstracting them.
The earliest version of this approach was
the SKI combinator calcul

data.title: How to configure X11 in a simple way
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何在使用X服务器而非Wayland的FreeBSD系统上，通过简单、成熟的老式工具和程序实现各种桌面环境效果，避免现代Linux桌面环境中常见的臃肿问题。文章涵盖了多个设置主题，包括：

1. **高分屏设置**：通过修改`xorg.conf`文件，根据显示器实际尺寸调整DPI，使GUI元素大小适中，避免眼部疲劳。
2. **键盘配置**：使用shell和文本编辑器完成。
3. **指向设备设置**：包括为左撇子用户配置轨迹球。
4. **屏幕保护程序**：使用经典的XScreenSaver。
5. **效果设置**：如透明度、阴影和动画，适用于轻量级窗口管理器如StumpWM。
6. **多显示器配置**：使用`xrandr`切换显示设置。
7. **显示管理器**：使用依赖较少的XDM。
8. **文件管理器和邮件客户端设置**：如使用Emacs Dired作为默认文件管理器。
9. **主题设置**：通过编辑文本文件实现，无需GUI工具。

文章强调通过成熟工具和方法实现功能，而不依赖大型桌面环境的框架和库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Wayland 取代 X11 后，系统配置的灵活性和易用性，以及用户对不同桌面环境和窗口管理器的偏好。

不同观点：
• [anonymousiam] 关注 Wayback 是否支持传统配置功能，特别是在 Wayland 取代 X11 的背景下，担心失去这些配置能力。
• [mid-kid] 提到当前使用 Xft.dpi 设置来调整 HiDPI，认为该方法适用于大多数应用程序，且操作简单。
• [snvzz] 表示已经转向 X11libre，暗示对 Xorg 被弃用后的替代方案有个人选择。
• [encom] 强烈反对手动编辑 xorg 配置文件，宁愿忍受一些软件的臃肿，也不愿再接触过去的复杂配置。
• [shmerl] 认为创建自定义 modelines 很麻烦，尤其是为了解决特定硬件和软件的兼容问题，暗示 Wayland 可能在这方面有所改进。
• [whalesalad] 以讽刺的方式回应长篇大论的讨论，暗示对复杂的技术讨论感到不满。
• [davydm] 表示不愿放弃现代桌面环境（如 KDE），即使有性能消耗，认为每个人的需求和偏好不同，不必过度优化。
• [cbondurant] 批评对轻量级窗口管理器的偏执态度，认为不应一味追求软件的纯粹性和完美，强调合理权衡的重要性，并指出讨论中的语气和错误。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于用户是否应该接受新技术的改变，特别是 Wayland 取代 X11 后，配置灵活性的丧失和易用性的提升之间的平衡。
• 对窗口管理器和桌面环境的选择存在分歧，部分用户喜欢轻量级和可配置性强的方案，而另一些用户则偏好功能丰富但可能更臃肿的现代桌面环境。
• 讨论中还涉及到对技术讨论的态度问题，特别是如何平衡技术纯粹性与实用性，以及在技术社区中如何进行建设性交流。

Preamble
The modern common Linux and as a result also a UNIX desktop is
heavily
bloated
. Even if you install not a full-scale DE like Gnome, but a
small WM: i3wm, WindowMaker, XFCE, StumpWM, etc. These window managers
are small itself, but when user installs a necessary GUI programs —
then a lot of
bloat
will be installed too: gsettings-daemon, D-Bus
daemon, polkitd, console-kit-daemon, etc, etc…
What can I do with all these
bloatware
? There are two solutions:
Disable unwanted compile-time options and recompile necessary stuff
by itself. I already wrote something about this approach
here
.
There is one disadvantage — sometimes you need to edit the source
code or port-related files to get rid of strange things, like
Krita's Wayland dependency when I'm using it in the pure X11
environment and so on.
Use good, old and mature, well-tested by time programs and
solutions. You don't obliged to install a lot of Gnome/KDE-related
libraries if you want a simple program with GUI to achieve a simple
task, like draw a login window and check user's credentials for the
single-user box.
In this post I'll write about the second approach — how to make nice
things with simple (for the "modern" world; of course some purist will
say that even
these
things are bloated too) good old programs and
ways.
All nice things from desktop environments, like nice effects, nice
themes, automatic execution of mail client after click on the proper
link, etc — don't need tons of frameworks and libraries from big
desktop environments. They are totally acessible with an elegant
utilities from a more civilized era.
Actions, described in this blogpost, were (obviously) performed in the
FreeBSD 14.3, not in Linux :-) and with X server, not Wayland :-).
Covered topics:
How to setup X server to operate with HighDPI display?
How to setup keyboard only with a shell and text editor?
How to setup different pointing devices, including tricky setup of
trackball for left-handed user?
Good old XScreenSaver.
How to setup nice effects: transparency, shadows and animations —
for a small WM (e.g. StumpWM)?
How to switch multi-monitor configurations and perform tricky things
with
xrandr
?
How to use XDM as a display manager and login screen? It has a very
limited set of dependencies, lesser than a "lightweight" LightDM.
How to use xdg-utils to open Emacs Dired as a default filemanager,
Emacs ComposeMode as a default e-mail composer, etc?
How to setup some nice themes without GUI utilities — just by
editing text files with any text editor?
High DPI
I have a small 13.3" display with a 2K resolultion in my laptop. As a
result, by default I see all GUI element on my screen very small, so I
can't see them without unnecessary strain in my eyes (and not only I,
of course).
The usual approach to this problem — instruct GUI environment that
this screen with a big resolution doesn't have a big diagonal too.
So, I read these articles:
HiDPI
in the ArchWiki
HOWTO set DPI in Xorg
And also a
man 5 xorg.conf
. Suddenly I found that I don't need to play
with tricky environment variables to please every GUI toolkit. All
that I need to do — is to specify active area dimensions in
millimeters for my monitor in X11 configuration! The neat part — this
settings will be applied to the whole system (login window, any WM,
etc), not only for logged in user with necessary environment
variables.
I got the necessary dimensions in millimeters from a display module
datasheet:
Active area dimensions (mm) from Sharp LQ125T1JW02 datasheet
And specified these dimensions in the proper section (file
/usr/local/etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/10-intel.conf
):
Section "Monitor"
Identifier  "MainMonitor"
Option      "Primary" "true"
DisplaySize 276.48 155.52
EndSection
The
MainMonitor
is specified in the
Device
section as monitor
connected to the DP-3 bus:
Section "Device"
Identifier  "intel"
...
Option      "Monitor-DP-3"   "MainMonitor"
Option      "Monitor-LVDS-1" "PhantomMonitor"
EndSection
And both sections are connected in the
Screen
section:
Section "Screen"
Identifier "MainScreen"
Device     "intel"
Monitor    "MainMonitor"
EndSection

本文介绍了如何在使用X服务器而非Wayland的FreeBSD系统上，通过简单、成熟的老式工具和程序实现各种桌面环境效果，避免现代Linux桌面环境中常见的臃肿问题。文章涵盖了多个设置主题，包括：

1. **高分屏设置**：通过修改`xorg.conf`文件，根据显示器实际尺寸调整DPI，使GUI元素大小适中，避免眼部疲劳。
2. **键盘配置**：使用shell和文本编辑器完成。
3. **指向设备设置**：包括为左撇子用户配置轨迹球。
4. **屏幕保护程序**：使用经典的XScreenSaver。
5. **效果设置**：如透明度、阴影和动画，适用于轻量级窗口管理器如StumpWM。
6. **多显示器配置**：使用`xrandr`切换显示设置。
7. **显示管理器**：使用依赖较少的XDM。
8. **文件管理器和邮件客户端设置**：如使用Emacs Dired作为默认文件管理器。
9. **主题设置**：通过编辑文本文件实现，无需GUI工具。

data.author: rpiguy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一种新型CGRA架构的效率、应用场景和潜在问题

不同观点：
• [pclmulqdq] 认为该架构类似于FPGA，但单元更大，效率在代码适合单一阵列时非常高，但当代码超出特定规模时，网格配置切换会消耗大量时间和功耗。
• [gamache] 指出该架构与GreenArray GA144相似，但担忧缺乏独特的FORTH方言可能影响市场接受度。
• [pedalpete] 质疑CPU是否真的是嵌入式设计中的能耗瓶颈，指出其他组件如扬声器和屏幕可能更耗电。
• [nnx] 认为该架构可能适合LLM推理，但疑惑为何未在这方面进行市场推广。
• [ACCount36] 认为该架构无法取代通用目的的Arm核心，但在低功耗优化和实时控制核心中可能有应用价值。
• [ZiiS] 对该架构在通用计算上比ARM更高效的可能性表示怀疑。
• [Grosvenor] 将其比作Itanium，指出静态调度和编译器优化的挑战。
• [archipelago123] 解释这是一种数据流架构，指出难以利用数据局部性，且现代乱序核心已解决了一些该架构试图解决的问题。
• [rpiguy] 比较该架构与Apple的神经引擎设计，质疑其在标量任务和多分支情况下的表现。
• [variadix] 对效率提升持保留态度，担心程序超出网格时的表现，并指出需要“足够聪明的编译器”，可能面临与FPGA类似的综合时间问题。

补充讨论：
• [Imustaskforhelp] 请求简化的解释。
• [kendalf89] 联想到编程游戏TIS-100。
• [icandoit] 提到与交互组合子的相似性，并讨论翻译层的构建。
• [vendiddy] 询问该架构是否类似于每个芯片上有多个小处理器。
• [wolfi1] 将其比作transputer架构的单硅片实现。

争议焦点：
• 该架构的实际能效和应用场景，尤其是在通用计算和特定领域（如LLM推理）中的潜力。
• 编译器优化和程序超出网格时的性能问题。

data.title: CO2 Battery
data.author: xnx
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种用于长时储能的CO2电池技术。该技术通过封闭的热机械转化过程，利用CO2在气液态之间的转换来发电，具有高效（往返效率75%以上）、成本效益高（具备竞争力的资本和运营支出）、灵活（可在全球任何地方建造）、耐用（30年以上无容量或性能衰减）、可靠（使用环保材料的现成组件）以及独立（不依赖锂等稀有金属）等优点。该技术已在兆瓦级工厂中得到验证并与电网连接。文中还提到Energy Dome公司的解决方案，通过从储气罐中抽取CO2并加压储存，然后通过涡轮机发电，实现长时储能。该技术被视为传统能源存储方案的替代选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新型长时储能技术（如基于二氧化碳的机械储能）的可行性、成本效益、技术细节及其与锂电池和压缩空气储能（CAES）等技术的比较。

不同观点：
• **成本与市场竞争**：
   - conradev指出，锂离子电池成本迅速下降，新技术的市场竞争风险大，尤其是需要大规模投资的情况下。同时，引用了Form Energy等公司面临的挑战。
   - epistasis强调，新的储能技术必须在某些指标上优于锂电池，尤其是成本效益（$/kWh）和循环效率等方面，才能在市场上立足。

• **是否为长时储能**：
   - credit_guy质疑该技术自称的“长时储能”标签，认为仅能存储8小时的能量并不能满足长时储能的需求，且若要具有经济性，长时储能应比短时储能便宜得多。
   - epistasis也指出，长时储能技术需要考虑充放电频率和能量泄漏等因素，以评估其经济潜力。

• **技术细节与数据透明度**：
   - gs17批评该技术的宣传材料缺乏具体数据，仅提供了一些模糊的参数，无法让潜在用户全面了解技术性能。
   - calmbonsai提出了一系列关键问题，包括能量密度、CapEx计算方法、充放电速率以及系统扩展能力等。

• **热力学与效率问题**：
   - nine_k从热力学角度质疑该技术的效率，尤其是气体膨胀时的吸热过程、压缩时的放热处理以及整体循环效率如何达到75%。
   - Peteragain同样对75%的循环效率表示怀疑，认为压缩机和涡轮机的效率组合难以达到如此高的水平。

• **环境与安全问题**：
   - darksaints担心大量二氧化碳集中存储可能带来的安全隐患，提到了历史上与二氧化碳相关的自然灾害。

• **与其他技术的比较**：
   - benlivengood提到该技术在高温差环境下可能带来的附加效益，如结合空调系统提升整体能效。
   - bee_rider和ricciardo则将该技术与压缩空气储能（CAES）进行比较，质疑其相对于锂电池和CAES的实际优势和缺点。

补充讨论：
• **市场潜力和技术多样性**：
   - datadrivenangel认为该技术具有潜力，因为它增加了储能技术的选择多样性，并可能降低对特定矿物的依赖，特别是在与太阳能结合使用时。

争议焦点：
• 该技术是否真正具备长时储能的经济性和效率，尤其是在与锂电池的竞争中。
• 技术细节不透明，导致外界对其性能和安全性的质疑。
• 热力学效率和安全性的争议，特别是二氧化碳的存储和使用是否会带来环境风险。

• **热力学与效率问题**：
   - nine_k从热力学角度质疑该技术的效率，尤其是气体膨胀时的吸热过程、压缩时的放热处理以及整体循环效率如何达到75%。
   - Peteragain同样对75%的循环效率表示怀疑，认为压缩机和涡轮机的效率组合难以达到如此高的水平。

• **环境与安全问题**：
   - darksaints担心大量二氧化碳集中存储可能带来的安全隐患，提到了历史上与二氧化碳相关的自然灾害。

• **与其他技术的比较**：
   - benlivengood提到该技术在高温差环境下可能带来的附加效益，如结合空调系统提升整体能效。
   - bee_rider和ricciardo则将该技术与压缩空气储能（CAES）进行比较，质疑其相对于锂电池和CAES的实际优势和缺点。

补充讨论：
• **市场潜力和技术多样性**：
   - datadrivenangel认为该技术具有潜力，因为它增加了储能技术的选择多样性，并可能降低对特定矿物的依赖，特别是在与太阳能结合使用时。

争议焦点：
• 该技术是否真正具备长时储能的经济性和效率，尤其是在与锂电池的竞争中。
• 技术细节不透明，导致外界对其性能和安全性的质疑。
• 热力学效率和安全性的争议，特别是二氧化碳的存储和使用是否会带来环境风险。

data.title: Nullable but not null
data.author: efeoge
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了后端应用中数据库模式演变时常见的一个问题：新增字段被设为可空（nullable），但在填充数据后未更新为非空（non-nullable），导致模式与实际数据不匹配。这可能引发混淆和不必要的复杂性，并使模式难以信任。为了解决此问题，作者提供了一个脚本，用于检查模型中的可空字段，并计算其中实际包含空值的行百分比。通过识别可以安全地改为非空字的段，开发者可以使数据模型更清晰、更安全。最终，确保数据库对必填字段的约束，有助于保持数据模型的准确性和应用的健康。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新字段是否应在数据库表中设置为可为空（nullable）

不同观点：
• nlitened和mdavid626支持新字段应默认为可为空，认为这更实际且能减少意外情况，因为新字段在系统中以前不存在，现在加入后也是可选的。他们强调，所有相关代码应能够处理字段为空的情况。
• stux指出，如果字段在领域模型中不应为空，且没有合理的默认值，则需要有其他方式表示“缺席”状态，类似于Swift中的非冻结枚举。
• codingdave和danbruc认为，判断字段是否应为可空需要综合考虑整个应用堆栈中的数据使用情况，而不仅仅是当前数据的状态。danbruc还提到，虽然可空但从未为空的列可能表明应为非空，但这并不是绝对的。
• deepsun和minkeymaniac提到更糟糕的情况，例如使用JSON存储数据导致字段可能缺失、为null或类型不一致，以及通过使用检查约束（check constraint）处理null问题。
• tudorg推荐使用工具如pgroll来自动化处理此类数据库变更问题。
• Trigg3r从SQL Server的角度分享了添加可空字段以避免破坏数百个存储过程的实际经验。
• PeterZaitsev质疑数据库设计是否应更注重在线、高效、非锁定地添加带有默认值的列，而不是让应用逻辑变得复杂和脆弱。
• lblume认为，可空字段表示数据可能为空，这与实际是否有空数据是不同的概念，强调了潜在性与现实性的区别。

补充讨论：
• jonny_eh建议在进行模式变更时使用检查清单。
• comrade1234和HocusLocus以较为调侃的语气表达了对长久以来技术妥协和捷径的不满，并暗示了对未来系统设计改进的期望。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于新字段是否应默认为可空，一方认为应默认可空以减少风险和意外，另一方认为应根据领域模型和数据使用情况决定是否可空，并探讨了处理“缺席”状态的更好方式。

44684168.article_content:
Back to all posts
Nullable but not null
When working on backend applications, especially those with evolving database schemas, it’s common to see a recurring pattern:
A new field is added to a model.
To avoid locking the table during the migration, the field is added as
nullable
.
The application logic is updated to start filling in this field.
A backfill job runs to populate the existing records.
The field is left as nullable.
People often forget the final step which is updating the schema to make the field non-nullable once the data is fully populated.
Why it matters
Leaving a field marked as nullable when it no longer contains nulls creates a mismatch between your schema and your actual data. This can lead to confusion, missed constraints and unnecessary complexity in your code. Over time, your schema becomes harder to trust. If a field is supposed to be required, your database should enforce it.
This happens because marking a field as non-nullable in production often requires care. Teams delay or skip it to avoid risk and the field stays nullable indefinitely. But a field that is
nullable in the schema
and
never null in practice is a silent lie
. This is a missed opportunity to make your data model clearer and safer.
How to fix it?
To help find these fields, I wrote a simple script that checks all models in a project. It scans for nullable fields and calculates how many rows actually contain null values. The idea is to identify cases where the field could safely be changed to non-nullable.
Here’s the code (written for Django, but the logic can be adapted to any ORM or raw SQL setup):
from
django.apps
import
apps
from
django.db
import
connection, transaction
def
get_nullable_fields
(model):
nullable_fields
=
[]
for
field
in
model._meta.fields:
if
getattr
(field,
'null'
,
False
)
and
not
field.auto_created:
nullable_fields.append(field.name)
return
nullable_fields
def
get_null_percentage_for_field
(model, field_name, total_rows):
if
total_rows
==
0
:
return
0.0
null_count
=
model.objects.filter(
**
{
f
"
{
field_name
}
__isnull"
:
True
}).count()
return
round
((null_count
/
total_rows)
*
100
,
2
)
def
analyze_all_models_fields_nulls_with_timeout
(timeout_ms
=
5000
):
"""
Analyze every nullable field in every model with a DB-level timeout in ms.
"""
results
=
[]
for
model
in
apps.get_models():
model_label
=
f
"
{
model._meta.app_label
}
.
{
model.
__name__}
"
with
connection.cursor()
as
cursor:
cursor.execute(
f
"SET LOCAL statement_timeout =
{
timeout_ms
}
;"
)
with
transaction.atomic():
nullable_fields
=
get_nullable_fields(model)
total_rows
=
model.objects.count()
if
total_rows
==
0
:
continue
for
field
in
nullable_fields:
null_percent
=
get_null_percentage_for_field(model, field, total_rows)
results.append({
"model"
: model_label,
"field"
: field,
"null_percentage"
: null_percent,
})
return
results
How to use it?
You can integrate this logic into a command-line tool, admin report, or health check. The output shows each nullable field and what percentage of rows actually contain nulls.
If a field has
0.0%
nulls, that’s a strong signal it should no longer be nullable. That change makes your schema more accurate, improves validation, and simplifies your codebase.
[
{
"model"
:
"users.Profile"
,
"field"
:
"birth_date"
,
"null_percentage"
:
0.0
},
{
"model"
:
"orders.Order"
,
"field"
:
"coupon_code"
,
"null_percentage"
:
92.4
},
{
"model"
:
"products.Product"
,
"field"
:
"description"
,
"null_percentage"
:
0.0
}
]
Final thoughts
Nullable fields that never hold nulls are often the result of incomplete migrations or forgotten cleanup steps. Catching and fixing them keeps your data model honest and your application healthier.
If a field is meant to be required, your database should say so. Nullable but not null? Time to clean that up.
Published: Jul 25, 2025

data.title: Neon Now Runs in VS Code
data.author: giladkleinman
data.article_summary: Neon推出了VS Code扩展插件“Neon Local Connect”，使开发者可以在IDE内更方便地使用Neon数据库进行本地开发。该工具通过静态localhost连接字符串，让用户在VS Code中直接管理Neon数据库分支、创建或重置分支、启动临时测试环境以及运行查询。它基于Neon Local的Docker代理，但无需手动设置CLI。用户可以轻松切换分支、隔离环境，并确保本地开发与团队同步，避免数据污染和架构漂移。通过该扩展，开发者可以一键登录Neon账户，选择或创建分支，并使用固定连接字符串连接到云端Neon数据库，实现类似本地Postgres的体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Serverless Postgres的实用性、成本及其相关工具或平台（如Neon）的使用体验

不同观点：
• princevegeta89认为Serverless Postgres在大多数情况下表现不佳，主要问题包括速度慢、延迟高，尤其在生产环境中的表现不尽如人意。他还指出，初创公司通常在前四年不需要考虑扩展性问题，过早优化扩展性没有意义，且Serverless Postgres的成本相对较高，不如使用每月约10美元的自托管Postgres服务或容器。

• mdaniel的评论主要集中在对Neon平台相关工具或代码的批评，带有情绪性地指责其许可协议和在GitHub上的代码发布方式。他提到一个具体的链接，并暗示该链接的内容不应被查看，带有对平台方的嘲讽态度。

• webdevver则对Neon平台的域名（neon.com）表示赞赏，认为拥有这样的域名会让公司更容易成功，表现出对平台未来前景的乐观预期。

补充讨论：
• princevegeta89的评论涉及了技术选型的成本与实用性问题，提出了自托管数据库服务作为Serverless Postgres的替代方案，具有实际的经济和性能考量。

• mdaniel的评论更多是针对许可协议和代码发布方式的法律或道德问题，情绪化较强，并没有深入讨论技术细节。

• webdevver的评论纯粹是基于域名印象的乐观预期，没有涉及技术细节或使用体验。

争议焦点：
• Serverless Postgres的性能、成本与实用性是主要争议点，尤其是在初创公司和技术开发者中的使用价值。
• Neon平台的工具发布方式及许可协议也引发了一些负面情绪，但更多是法律和道德层面的讨论，而非技术本身。

44640618.article_content:
Workflows
Jul 21, 2025
Neon Now Runs in VS Code
Branch, test, and reset from your IDE using Neon Local Connect
Developers love using Neon branches for a local development, due to the agility they provide (e.g. fast resets, isolated environments, and the ability to test without polluting production data). But using Neon branches still requires you to manage separate connection strings for different branches and ensure your application and its environment is properly set up to connect.
Today, that gets a lot easier, especially if you’re a VS Code user!
We’re launching
Neon Local Connect
, a new VS Code extension that connects your Neon database to your local dev environment using a static
localhost
connection string.
You can browse your tables, create or reset branches, launch ephemeral test environments, and run queries all from inside your IDE.Behind the scenes, the extension builds on
Neon Local
, our open-source Docker proxy for connecting to Neon over
localhost
. But now, it’s fully integrated into VS Code, no CLI setup required.
Branching That Feels Local
Running Postgres locally works – until you need it to stay in sync with the rest of your team.
You’re responsible for installing the right version, managing credentials, seeding realistic data, resetting state between test runs, and isolating changes from other projects on your machine. If you’re working in a team, there’s no guarantee your local database matches production or even your teammate’s dev environment. Schema drift is common. Rollbacks are manual. Spinning up a clean environment means rebuilding everything from scratch.
That’s why
Neon branches
help so much with this workflow. In case you’re not familiar with them, a
branch
in Neon is a full, isolated copy of your database created instantly from any parent. It has great potential for improving local workflows:
It gives you a clean slate for every feature, test, or teammate
With zero risk of corrupting production or shared dev data (branches are isolated and have their own compute endpoint)
You can reset instantly to a known schema and data snapshot, avoiding drift
They let you test migrations in isolation, then throw them away (they’re great as ephemeral environments)
This is all great, but if you want to start using Neon branches as your “local” Postgres, connecting your app to those branches required a bit of work (wiring up credentials, managing TLS, switching tools). We first built
Neon Local
to help, but it still required Docker setup and scripting.
With Neon Local Connect,
you can connect to any branch directly from your editor, using a static localhost connection string. It behaves exactly like a local Postgres instance, but backed by Neon’s serverless cloud and branching engine.
How Neon Local Connect Works
Behind the scenes, this extension is using a Docker-based local proxy (via
Neon Local
) to route traffic from localhost to your Neon database branch. The extension handles authentication, networking, and branch selection for you. All you have to do is select which branch you want to connect to and run your application.
Here’s what the workflow looks like:First, you install the extension from the
VS Code Marketplace
. Once you’ve done that, you sign in with your Neon account. You can use OAuth for a fast, one-click login using your browser, or provide an API key if you want finer-grained access or plan to use ephemeral branches (which require long-lived credentials for cleanup). Once authenticated, the extension fetches your Neon projects and branches so you can quickly connect to an existing environment or create a new one on the fly.
Once you’re in, you can pick a branch from your Neon project or create a new one directly from the extension by choosing a parent branch and giving it a name:
Then, click Connect:
The extension launches a local Docker container that exposes a static Postgres connection at
localhost:5432
. Your app connects using a fixed connection string:
From your app’s point of view, it’s talking to a local Postgres database – but in reality, all traffic is routed to the Neon branch you selected hosted in the cloud.
You can commit the static
localhost
connection string to your project’s repo or CI config, and easily swap between branches in your IDE as needed.
What You Can Do With It
This extension turns your editor into a control panel for your Neon database.
Create new branches on the fly
Need a fresh environment for a new feature, teammate, or experiment? You can create a new branch directly in the extension UI. Just give it a name and choose a parent branch (e.g. main). Your new branch will be provisioned instantly, with the same schema and data as the parent. This is a frictionless way to isolate work without stepping on shared environments.
Query your database

data.author: XnoiVeX
data.article_summary: 《旧金山互联网档案馆成为联邦寄存图书馆：意义何在？》一文报道了位于旧金山的互联网档案馆获得联邦寄存图书馆资格，加入了一个由超过1,100家图书馆组成的网络，这些图书馆负责保存并向公众提供政府文件。在加州参议员亚历克斯·帕迪拉的指定下，互联网档案馆获得此资格，将有助于扩大联邦政府出版物的数字化访问。互联网档案馆创始人布鲁斯特·卡赫表示，此举使档案馆能更方便地与其他联邦寄存图书馆合作，服务公众。尽管档案馆面临法律挑战，如其开放图书馆因电子书借阅问题被起诉，但它仍致力于数字化政府文件，并通过“民主图书馆”项目进一步推动其使命。这一新资格将帮助互联网档案馆更便捷地获取和分享政府资料。

SF-Based Internet Archive Is Now a Federal Depository Library. What Does That Mean?
Morgan Sung
Jul 24
Save Article
Save Article
Failed to save article
Please try again
Email
Various types of electronics sit on a shelf at the Internet Archive offices in San Francisco on March 24, 2023. The Internet Archive, thanks to its designation by California Sen. Alex Padilla, joins a network of over 1,100 libraries that make government documents accessible to the public.
(Beth LaBerge/KQED)
The San Francisco-based
Internet Archive
now has federal depository status, joining a network of over 1,100 libraries that archive government documents and make them accessible to the public — even as ongoing legal challenges pose an existential threat to the organization.
California Sen. Alex Padilla made the designation in
a letter
sent Thursday to the Government Publishing Office, which
oversees the program
. In the letter, shared exclusively with KQED, Padilla praised the Internet Archive for its “digital focus” and said it “is leading the way when it comes to providing online library services.”
“The Archive’s digital-first approach makes it the perfect fit for a modern federal depository library, expanding access to federal government publications amid an increasingly digital landscape,” Padilla said in a statement to KQED. “The Internet Archive has broken down countless barriers to accessing information, and it is my honor to provide this designation to help further their mission of providing ‘Universal Access to All Knowledge.’”
Sponsored
Under federal law, members of Congress can designate up to two qualified libraries for federal depository status.
Internet Archive founder Brewster Kahle said that while the nonprofit organization has always functioned as a library, this new designation makes it easier to work with the other federal depository libraries. That, he said, is a service to everyone.
Brewster Kahle closes a storage container with books from the Allen County Public Library at an Internet Archive storage facility in Richmond on March 30.
(Beth LaBerge/KQED)
“ I think there is a great deal of excitement to have an organization such as the Internet Archive, which has physical collections of materials, but is really known mostly for being accessible as part of the internet,” Kahle said. “And helping integrate these materials into things like Wikipedia, so that the whole internet ecosystem gets stronger as digital learners get closer access into the government materials.”
The Federal Depository Library Program was established by Congress in 1813, with the intention of ensuring that government records would be accessible to the American public. It includes maps, environmental reports, health studies, congressional records, newspapers and books.
These records account for “millions and millions of pages” that can take up entire floors of public libraries, Kahle said. San Diego’s public library
gave up its federal depository status
in 2020 because its government documents took up so much space and often went unused.
While documents stored on microfiche or microfilm are easy to copy, they aren’t easy to access. The GPO has been moving toward digital preservation since 2016 and runs an
online database
of government records, and in recent years, it has
ramped up efforts
to digitize the Federal Depository Library Program.
Participating libraries have largely pivoted to the GPO’s digital approach, but digitizing countless physical documents is a massive undertaking — one that the Internet Archive has experience with.
For years, the Internet Archive has helped libraries and other academic institutions in digitizing their collections and hosting them online. In 2022, it launched
Democracy’s Library
, a free online compendium of government research and publications.
Joining the Federal Depository Library Program is the next step in the evolution of Democracy’s Library, Kahle said. The Archive is “just doing what it’s always been doing,” but now, it’s more convenient.
“By being part of the program itself, it just gets us closer to the source of where the materials are coming from, so that it’s more reliably delivered to the Internet Archive, to then be made available to the patrons of the Internet Archive or partner libraries,” he continued.
Laura Gibbs looks at memorabilia at the Internet Archive offices in San Francisco.
(Beth LaBerge/KQED)
The organization has faced legal challenges over some of its archival practices. Its Open Library was at the center of a yearslong
legal battle
after four major publishers sued the Internet Archive for
temporarily lifting its waitlists
in 2020 — instead of loaning its digital copies to one user at a time. By doing so, the publishers alleged, the Internet Archive illegally provided free e-books.
Last year, an appeals court upheld a 2023 federal court decision that ruled against the Internet Archive. The organization has had to remove more than half a million titles
